narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Crossing"**

The docs site is the Cerberus design system wearing its own clothes. Every color, type style, radius and shadow is a Panda semantic token from `@cerberus/panda-preset`, so the site has no palette of its own: it has four. Cerberus, Acheron, Elysium and Oceanus each ship light and dark modes, and the visitor's active theme paints every surface.

The home page is one journey across one painting: Joachim Patinir's *Landscape with Charon Crossing the Styx* (c. 1520–24, Museo Nacional del Prado, public domain). Its places are the four themes and the four parts of the ecosystem: Elysium's angels (Design), the sea on the horizon (Foundation), Charon's ferry on the river (Build) and Cerberus at the gate (Agents), then the far shore. Scroll is the camera. A fixed WebGL stage renders the painting with a living river, a focus pull and a soft-light grade in the current realm's own hue, and the page's own `page.bg.initial` veils it for reading. Poppins sets the type at poster scale over it, and each realm's proof is a live plate of real components rendered in that realm's theme.

The hex values below are the **Cerberus theme** reference values (dark mode unless named "daylight"), recorded so tools can render swatches. Code never uses them: it uses the semantic token names given with each color.
keyCharacteristics: Four themes, one token vocabulary: `page.*`, `action.*` and the status palettes resolve per theme under `data-panda-theme` and the `dark` / `light` / `system` classes.
Realms are theme-scoped subtrees: a plate or probe sets `data-panda-theme="<realm>"` and its `action.*` tokens become that realm's hue.
The painting is the world: one camera over one public-domain image, with a still poster that takes the same framing whenever WebGL or motion is unavailable.
Poster-scale Poppins over the painting; copy reads on feathered pools of page color, never on boxes.
Live proof: real, controlled Cerberus components in every chapter, never screenshots.
Recursive is used only for code.

rules.name: The Token-Only Rule
rules.body: Color is written as a semantic token name, never a hex, in every component. The hexes here are swatch references for the Cerberus theme; the same token is gold, teal or blue in another theme.

rules.name: The Realm Scope Rule
rules.body: A realm hue appears by scoping, not by naming. Wrap the subtree in `data-panda-theme="<realm>"` and use `action.*`; never reach for another theme's hue by value. Cerberus needs `staticCss.themes: ['cerberus']` to be scopable inside another active theme.

rules.name: The Painting Grades, the Page Veils Rule
rules.body: The world's hue grade comes only from the realm's own `action.bg.initial`, read from the DOM; its veil comes only from `page.bg.initial`. Change the theme and the painting follows with no code change.

rules.name: The One Actor Rule
rules.body: Within any one theme scope, `action.*` is the only hue that acts. Status palettes signal status; they never decorate.

rules.name: The Poster Scale Rule
rules.body: Display type over the painting uses only the four clamps above, with negative em tracking between -0.03em and -0.06em and line height at or under 1.06. Never add a fifth size or a second display face.

rules.name: The Mono-for-Code Rule
rules.body: Recursive is set with `fontFamily: 'mono'` on top of a Poppins label or body text style (`label-sm`, `body-sm`, `body-md`) and only for code: package names, install commands, token names, file names and inline code. The `mono-*` text styles are reserved for numbers in data visualization and are not used for UI copy.

rules.name: The Balanced Heading Rule
rules.body: Headings use `textWrap: 'balance'`; paragraphs use `textWrap: 'pretty'`. Numbers that change or align get `fontVariantNumeric: 'tabular-nums'`.

rules.name: The Feathered Pool Rule
rules.body: Copy over the painting reads on a pool of page color, never a box: an absolutely positioned, `aria-hidden` span behind the text with `radial-gradient(closest-side, …)` of `page.bg.initial` (about 80% at the center, transparent at the edge), centered inside its own box and inset beyond the text so it fades out before any edge shows. Realm names, chapter copy, the hero strip and the diptych caption all use it.

rules.name: The One Lift Rule
rules.body: A surface that holds live components gets `shadow.2xl` and a 1px `action.border.initial` edge in its realm's theme; copy never gets a surface or a shadow.

rules.name: The Reachable Reveal Rule
rules.body: Reveals animate opacity and transform only, never `visibility` or `display`; anything already on screen is never hidden, and a plate's reveal finishes at once on `focusin`, so every control stays keyboard reachable.

rules.name: The Still Poster Rule
rules.body: Under `prefers-reduced-motion`, on the server and before hydration there is no smooth scroll, no camera and no canvas: the painting is a still poster and every section renders in its final state.

dos: **Do** write color as semantic tokens and type as text styles or the four display clamps; the hexes in this file are Cerberus-theme references only.
**Do** color a realm by scoping a subtree with `data-panda-theme="<realm>"` and using `action.*` inside it.
**Do** check every surface in all four themes and in light, dark and system modes, with WebGL on and off.
**Do** set copy over the painting on a feathered `radial-gradient(closest-side, …)` pool of `page.bg.initial`.
**Do** show real, controlled Cerberus components on live plates with `shadow.2xl` and the realm's `action.border.initial` edge.
**Do** route all scroll motion through the one Lenis engine and GSAP, with a still poster and final states under reduced motion.
**Do** credit the painting where it is shown, and keep provenance beside every shipped raster.
donts: **Don't** hard-code a hex, rgb or pixel value in component styles; use the token, or add one to the preset.
**Don't** use Recursive for anything but code, and don't use the `mono-*` text styles for UI copy.
**Don't** put copy over the painting in a hard-edged box or a full-width dark band; feather it.
**Don't** add a second smooth-scroll engine, or hide a revealed element with `visibility`.
**Don't** use a status palette (`success`, `warning`, `info`, `danger`) for decoration.
**Don't** replace a working component with a picture of it.
